title: How the Heart Pumps Blood Around the Body

beats.title: The two-circuit map
beats.script: Draw the heart as a central four-chamber shape. Draw the lungs above it and the body tissues around it. Add blue arrows from the heart to the lungs and red arrows from the lungs to the heart. Add red arrows from the heart to the body and blue arrows back to the heart.

beats.title: The four chambers and main vessels
beats.script: Divide the heart into four labeled chambers. Draw the venae cavae entering the right atrium. Draw the pulmonary artery leaving the right ventricle. Draw the pulmonary veins entering the left atrium and the aorta leaving the left ventricle.

beats.title: Valves enforce one-way flow
beats.script: Draw the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and right ventricle. Draw the pulmonary valve at the exit of the right ventricle. beats.script: Shade both relaxed ventricles as filling spaces. Draw blue blood entering the right atrium through the venae cavae. Draw red blood entering the left atrium through the pulmonary veins. Add arrows through the open tricuspid and mitral valves into both ventricles.

beats.title: Ventricular contraction
beats.script: Draw thick walls squeezing both ventricles. Mark the tricuspid and mitral valves closed with short bars. Draw the pulmonary and aortic valves open. Add blue and red arrows shooting out through the pulmonary artery and aorta.

beats.title: Gas exchange in the lungs
beats.script: Draw a small alveolus beside a web of pulmonary capillaries. Label blue blood arriving from the pulmonary artery. Draw carbon dioxide arrows from the blood into the alveolus. Draw oxygen arrows into the blood and red blood leaving toward the pulmonary veins.

beats.title: Delivery to body tissues
beats.script: Draw the aorta branching into arteries that reach a body-tissue capillary bed. Add oxygen and nutrient arrows from the capillaries into nearby cells. Add carbon dioxide and waste arrows from the cells back into the capillaries. Draw veins collecting the blue blood and returning it toward the venae cavae.

beats.title: One heartbeat, one complete route
beats.script: Trace one continuous blue arrow from the body through the venae cavae, right atrium, right ventricle, and pulmonary artery. Continue the route through the lungs, changing the arrow to red as it enters the pulmonary veins and left atrium. Draw the red route through the left ventricle and aorta to the body tissues. Label filling at the atria and ventricles, squeezing at the ventricles, and place valve symbols along the one-way path.
